minutes.headline: Open Space Committee backed title certification for Lake Shirley parcel 137-12; chair resigned with no successor.
minutes.summary: The committee recommended the town not exercise first refusal on a Chapter 61A parcel at 490 Chase Road, and recommended the Select Board pursue title certification on map 137 parcel 12. Bob reported on conservation parcel records and new trail kiosks, and the chair announced his resignation with no volunteer to replace him. The committee also discussed how to spend a $10,000 grant and set the next meeting for February 8.

budget_items.what_was_said: The state had indicated willingness to help fund a car-top boat launch on parcel 12 if the town shows clear title; a member says state funds exist for it.
Town counsel reportedly said the cost of a title search varies greatly by parcel, so certifying one parcel would reveal the likely cost.
The chair would resist seeking town appropriation for the remaining Lane parcel but supports pointing land trusts to it for a grant-funded acquisition.
A grant was received that the committee reads as giving it discretion to spend. It was suggested to confirm account restrictions with the town finance official and to spend it on one big project.

decisions.decision: Results of the parcel 12 vote to be communicated to Paula; other parcels' title questions to be taken up at a later meeting.
Chair will consult Adam Bernie on how to handle the chairmanship since no one volunteered; vice chair offered by one member.
Next meeting set for February 8 at 7:30 pm, after scheduling conflicts ruled out other dates.
Grant spending to go on an upcoming agenda; a member will speak with Heather about how the account is set up.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee voted, all four members aye, to recommend the Select Board pursue title certification of parcel 137-12 near Lake Shirley.
The committee voted unanimously to recommend the town not exercise its right of first refusal on the 490 Chase Road Chapter 61A withdrawal.
The chair announced his resignation; no member volunteered, and he will consult staff on how to handle the chairmanship.
Members discussed how to use a grant received for open space, and agreed to put it on a future agenda after checking the account's restrictions.
The next meeting was set for February 8 at 7:30 pm.

why_it_matters: Title certification on the Lake Shirley parcel could show what a title search costs and may open the way to state grant money for a car-top boat launch, which would affect town-owned land and any future spending on it.
With no chair and a gap of nearly two months until the next meeting, the committee's recommendations on land and grant spending may be slow to reach the Select Board.
